TEXT.English:
Complexity: Advanced[NEWLINE]The Chimar must decide what they want to build in their cities from the moment new cities are built. Be mindful of your selections!
[ICON_BULLET]1: Your capital should be Muris (recon) or Scorpion (archery) for the easiest start. Neith (magic) at least gets you 3 power units. Lukos (mounted) is the most challenging start.
[ICON_BULLET]2: Early defense can be difficult for the Chimar - don't be afraid to build more goblins than the norm. Remember that you can build defensive melee in any city if needed.
[ICON_BULLET]3: Your unique worker, [LINK=UNIT_GRETCHIN]Gretchin[\LINK], costs no food to produce but is less effective than other workers and gets no experience. They do have attack power, so if an enemy attacks a stack of gretchin only one will die. You will want a lot of gretchin.
[ICON_BULLET]4: Flat worker-boosters are expecially valuable to the Chimar. These include the spell [LINK=SPELL_ENCHANTED_BLADE]enchanted blade[\LINK] (Enchantment), or the resources [LINK=BONUS_STONE]stone[\LINK] ([LINK=TECH_MASONRY]masonry[\LINK]) or [LINK=BONUS_OBSIDIAN]obsidian[\LINK] ([LINK=TECH_CONSTRUCTION]construction[\LINK]).
[ICON_BULLET]5: It's a good idea to have multiple clan cities around for flexibility, but you don't always need all of them. Try to focus on one or two clans - if you're relying on defensive melee, you might not need a Scorpion city; whereas if you lack [LINK=TECH_STIRRUPS]stirrups[\LINK], a Lukos city may not help as much as another city that can produce [LINK=UNIT_RANGER]rangers[\LINK].
[ICON_BULLET]6: Neith cities are good at science (Only they can build [LINK=BUILDING_ALCHEMY_LAB]alchemy labs[\LINK]), and thus are good choices for island cities or other high-commerce-low-production areas.
[ICON_BULLET]7: Remember that religious units can help cover you. Most religious units can replace defensive melee for purposes of defense, enabling you to continue focusing down the tech line that you're trying to specialize in.
[ICON_BULLET]8: With [LINK=TRAIT_WARLORD]Warlord[\LINK]/[LINK=TRAIT_CHARISMATIC]Charismatic[\LINK], [LINK=LEADER_GOBLIN]Gurlug[\LINK] is good at helping goblins grow from battles - take advantage of this even if it's a touch risky. Success will get bolstered by [LINK=PROMOTION_AMBITION]ambition[\LINK] and being charismatic.
Author - Kantolin

TEXT.English: More and more attention has been given to Lukos clan cities recently due to their interesting horse games. Most of these games started as simple games that the Lukos encourage their youths to play, but some are becoming full fledged sports with increasingly firm and ritualized rules. The effect on Lukos military units has been positive as well, as the most recent generation of Lukos are naturally talented. This may be the best moment for you to step into the situation.

TEXT.English: This has happened far too often to be a coincidence - something is wrong with Scorpion clan's bows. You've spent the past week meeting with Scorpion clan leaders - they are now assuming sabotage, fortunately from out of the Confederation. These discussions have shown just how much attention the Scorpion clan spends on their bows - and their poison, yes, but the bows and arrows that deliver the poison as well.

TEXT.English: A new group of Muris clan youths are coming of age, and there's a small problem of their focus. Exploration- that's easy and by this point in their training comes naturally enough... but mapmaking is something almost this entire slew of troops is increasingly poor at. They avoid it when they can, and rush it otherwise. Elder Muris expect them to grow out of this problem, but it hasn't happened yet...

TEXT.English: Given how central Muris culture is to the Chimar, encouraging an apprentice system might work. That way the young muris can learn mapmaking from their elders - and learn a bit about modern recon tricks. Between the maps and the scouting, Muris clan cities will become even more of the backbone of the Chimar.

TEXT.English: As all know, the Muris Clan was an early supporter of the Confederacy, and was rewarded for its loyalty with the control of large urban territories. While a fine political move, it was reviled by my colleagues studying urban planning. Indeed, the Muris' idea of architecture is a bunch of felled trees cobbled together, and their understanding of hygiene is whatever makes their rodent hordes thrive. i've long held the belief it's why they make the best scouts in the Confederacy. The wilderness is vastly preferable to sitting at home when home is in a Muris City.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]--Extract from History of the Confederacy, Tarnat the Ever-Quoted
